note: Conceptual arrangement comparison. The baseline is the current illustrative site assignment. Scenarios B and C are schematic propositions, not georeferenced plans, surveys or construction layouts. No scenario is a winner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Distributed woodland retreats
scenarios.summary: Keep the six homes dispersed across the property, each with its own relationship to rock, trees and view. The lodge remains near the entrance and shared parking.
advantages: Greater separation and visual privacy between households.
Individual orientations and distinct identities for each home.
Shared outdoor life is optional rather than constantly visible.
disadvantages: Possible additional ecological disturbance from paths and services.
evaluationQuestions: Can every home reach the lodge and a shared outdoor place without a car?
Are the paths short and legible enough for ordinary visits?
Does dispersal protect privacy without making shared life impractical?

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Shared central clearing
scenarios.summary: Arrange the homes around a recognisable common clearing with the lodge and shared outdoor rooms at the centre.
advantages: Communal activity is visible and easy to reach.
Shorter connections between homes and common facilities.
disadvantages: Noise and activity concentrate in one place.
The clearing may disturb sensitive land or existing trees.
The arrangement may feel suburban rather than woodland-based.
evaluationQuestions: Can a resident withdraw without feeling watched?
Does the central clearing damage a sensitive ecological feature?
Can the lodge be used for one small task without joining an event?

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Woodland spine with social pockets
scenarios.summary: Retain dispersed homes but connect them with a clear pedestrian spine and several modest shared pockets rather than one central clearing.
advantages: Balances privacy with repeat social contact.
The walking experience can respond to terrain and trees.
Small shared places can be maintained in stages.
disadvantages: Routes may conflict with private edges and winter access.
A spine can become a corridor if it is over-designed.
evaluationQuestions: Does the spine connect real destinations rather than passing private windows?
Can each pocket be used by one or two people without booking an event?
Is the route usable in winter and by people with reduced mobility?
